name: Zeto + Regulator (KYC)
tagline: ZK transfer — amounts hidden from everyone, even the Regulator; who gates participation by KYC
concept: A zero-knowledge Zeto transfer with no notary and no hook. The Regulator is the KYC authority: it admits or blocks participants (every transfer's ZK proof must prove sender & recipient are registered). But Zeto hides amounts from everyone except the owning party — so the Regulator gates WHO may transact, yet can see neither how much nor between whom. Other consortium members and the public see only ZK commitments/nullifiers.

consortium.name: Consortium member
consortium.role: On the chain · not a participant

steps.title: Regulator deploys a KYC-gated Zeto token & admits the banks
steps.plain: The Regulator deploys a zero-knowledge Zeto token (no notary) and registers Bank A and Bank B in the on-chain KYC registry. An un-admitted party can't transact — its transfer proof would fail.

steps.title: Regulator issues 1,000 to Bank A
steps.plain: The Regulator mints the initial supply to Bank A. Only Bank A can decrypt the resulting note — not even the Regulator who issued it can read the amount.
steps.tech: zeto.mint({ to: bankA, amount: 1000 })  ·  ZK commitment on-chain

steps.title: Bank A transfers 300 to Bank B
steps.plain: Bank A sends 300 to Bank B. The ZK proof shows both are KYC-registered and value is conserved — without revealing the amount or the parties. Only Bank A and Bank B see their own notes; the Regulator, other members and the public see only a nullifier + commitment.
steps.tech: zeto.transfer({ to: bankB, amount: 300 })  ·  nullifier + ZK commitment

facts.title: KYC registry (authority)
facts.detail: admits / blocks participants · cannot see amounts

facts.title: Transfer recorded
facts.detail: nullifier + ZK commitment · amount & parties hidden
